description: When the local service is down, the in-form error headline is the raw browser string 'Failed to fetch'.
expected: 'Pardner couldn't reach your local service. Your task is saved and will be sent when you retry.'
actual: 'Failed to fetch' / 'Your last confirmed data remains available.'
suggested_fix: Map TypeError/network failures to a human message that names the local service and the saved request.

description: While a create is pending, Create task stays enabled and primary-styled; clicking it sends nothing and replaces the original error with 'Resolve the saved request before starting another change.', hiding the cause.
expected: Create task disabled (or relabelled) while a request is pending; Retry saved request is the single primary action.
actual: disabled=false, class 'primary'; second click swaps the error text.
suggested_fix: Disable Create task while pending and give Retry saved request primary styling; keep the original cause visible.

criterion: Information stated once / one way per task
description: During an outage the page shows three status messages and two retry buttons at once: header 'Local service disconnected', banner 'The local Pardner client did not respond…' with Retry connection, and 'A request is awaiting confirmation.' with Retry saved request.
expected: One outage notice with one Retry that reconnects and then resends the saved request.
actual: Two stacked banners plus header status, two retry buttons.
suggested_fix: Merge into one notice; Retry reconnects and replays the pending operation; once the service is back, auto-retry the pending (idempotent) operation.

description: After the service comes back the header recovers to 'Saved locally · synced', but the pending create is not resent automatically and New task stays disabled until the person clicks Retry saved request, even though the operation is idempotent (same operationId).
expected: Idempotent pending operation retried automatically on reconnect.
suggested_fix: On successful reconnect, replay the stored pending operation once; keep manual retry as fallback.
